'''Eleni Diamanti''' is a Greek engineer who is a researcher at the [[French National Centre for Scientific Research]] (CNRS). Diamanti serves as Director of the Paris Centre for Quantum Computing. She was awarded a [[European Research Council]] Starting Grant in 2018.

== Early life and education ==
Diamanti is from Greece. She was an undergraduate student at the [[National Technical University of Athens]], where she majored in electrical and computer engineering.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Lead Scientists {{!}} QCALL|url=http://www.qcall-itn.eu/people/lead-scientists/|access-date=2021-06-27|language=en-GB}}</ref> She moved to the [[United States]] for graduate studies, joining [[Stanford University]] as a Master's student. She remained at Stanford for her doctoral research, where she looked at the implementation of phase shift quantum key distribution systems.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Physics - Eleni Diamanti|url=https://physics.aps.org/authors/eleni_diamanti|access-date=2021-06-27|website=physics.aps.org}}</ref> After graduating, Diamanti returned to [[Europe]], where she joined [[Institut d'Optique]] as a [[Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions]] Fellow.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Eleni Diamanti's Home Page|url=http://www-soc.lip6.fr/~ediamanti/cv.html|access-date=2021-06-27|website=www-soc.lip6.fr}}</ref> She completed her habilitation at the [[Paris Diderot University]] in 2014. 

== Research and career ==
Diamanti was appointed to the faculty at the [[French National Centre for Scientific Research]] (CNRS) in 2009. Her research considers experimental quantum cryptography and the development of photonics sources for quantum networks.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Speaker Details: CyberSecure|url=https://emtech.technologyreview.com/cyber-secure-2020/speaker/164170/eleni-diamanti|access-date=2021-06-27|website=emtech.technologyreview.com|language=en-AG|archive-date=2021-06-27|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210627202301/https://emtech.technologyreview.com/cyber-secure-2020/speaker/164170/eleni-diamanti|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=QUSCO|url=https://issuu.com/euresearcher/docs/eu_research_23_digital_magazine/s/10728922|access-date=2021-06-27|website=issuu}}</ref> Alongside developing encryption software using quantum technology, Diamanti was made Vice Director of the Paris Center for Quantum Computing. In this capacity she takes part in the [[European Union]] Quantum Flagship.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Wills|first=Stewart|title=EuroQuantum|url=https://www.osa-opn.org/home/articles/volume_29/september_2018/features/euroquantum/|url-status=live|access-date=2021-06-27|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190125030237/https://www.osa-opn.org/home/articles/volume_29/september_2018/features/euroquantum/ |archive-date=2019-01-25 }}</ref> She was awarded a Prime d'Excellence Scientifique from the CNRS in 2013. In 2018 Diamanti was awarded a [[European Research Council]] Starting Grant.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Quantum superiority with coherent states|url=https://cordis.europa.eu/project/id/758911|url-status=live|access-date=2021-06-27|website=European Research Council|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210627202302/https://cordis.europa.eu/project/id/758911 |archive-date=2021-06-27 }}</ref> In 2024 she received the Innovation Medal by the CNRS.<ref>{{Cite web |date=Jul 2024 |title=Trio gagnant pour l'innovation |url=https://lejournal.cnrs.fr/nos-blogs/de-la-decouverte-a-linnovation/trio-gagnant-pour-linnovation |access-date=2024-07-19 |website=CNRS Le journal |language=fr}}</ref>
